ja: 「ウォール・ストリート・ジャーナル」は1889年創刊。株価指数のダウ平均を考えたチャールズ・ダウが創刊者の一人。
easy: The Wall Street Journal started in 1889. One of its founders, Charles Dow, also created the Dow stock index.
std: The Wall Street Journal was first published in 1889; one of its founders, Charles Dow, also created the Dow Jones Industrial Average.

ja: ダウ平均株価に最初に採用された銘柄のうち、長く残ったのはゼネラル・エレクトリックだったが、2018年に外された。
easy: General Electric was in the Dow index for over 100 years, until 2018.
std: General Electric was the last of the original Dow Jones Industrial Average companies to remain in the index, until it was removed in 2018.

ja: 行動経済学の研究で、ダニエル・カーネマンは2002年、リチャード・セイラーは2017年にノーベル経済学賞を受けた。
easy: Two scientists who studied how people really make money decisions won Nobel Prizes, in 2002 and 2017.
std: Pioneers of behavioral economics won Nobel Prizes: Daniel Kahneman in 2002 and Richard Thaler in 2017.

ja: 「損失回避」：人は同じ額でも、得をする喜びより損をする痛みを約2倍強く感じる傾向があるとされる。
easy: People often feel the pain of losing money about twice as strongly as the joy of winning the same amount.
std: Loss aversion describes how people tend to feel losses roughly twice as strongly as gains of the same size.

ja: 「アンカリング効果」：最初に見た数字が、その後の判断に強く影響する。値引き前の価格が書いてあると安く感じるのもこのため。
easy: The first number we see affects our later choices. This is called the anchoring effect.
std: The anchoring effect means the first number we encounter strongly influences later judgments, which is why a crossed-out 'original price' makes a sale price look cheap.

ja: ジャムの試食実験では、24種類並べたときより6種類のときのほうが、実際に買う人の割合がずっと高かった。選択肢が多すぎると選べなくなる例として知られる。
easy: In one study, more people bought jam when there were 6 kinds than when there were 24 kinds.
std: In a well-known study, shoppers offered 6 jams were far more likely to buy than those offered 24, an example of 'choice overload'.

ja: 「サンクコスト（埋没費用）」は、もう取り戻せない費用のこと。それにこだわって損を続けてしまうことを「サンクコストの誤り」と呼ぶ。
easy: A 'sunk cost' is money you already spent and cannot get back. Good decisions should not depend on it.
std: A sunk cost is money already spent that cannot be recovered; continuing a failing project because of it is known as the sunk cost fallacy.

ja: アダム・スミスの『国富論』は1776年に出版された。分業によってピン工場の生産量が大きく増える例が有名。
easy: Adam Smith's famous book 'The Wealth of Nations' came out in 1776.
std: Adam Smith's 'The Wealth of Nations', published in 1776, famously used a pin factory to show how the division of labor raises productivity.

ja: 「見えざる手」はアダム・スミスの言葉として有名だが、『国富論』の中でこの表現が出てくるのは1回だけ。
easy: Adam Smith's phrase 'invisible hand' is very famous, but it appears only once in 'The Wealth of Nations'.
std: Although 'the invisible hand' is closely associated with Adam Smith, the phrase appears only once in 'The Wealth of Nations'.

ja: 『エコノミスト』誌のビッグマック指数は、各国のビッグマックの値段を比べて通貨の割安・割高を見る指標。1986年に始まった。
easy: The Big Mac Index compares the price of a Big Mac in different countries to see if money is cheap or expensive.
std: The Economist's Big Mac Index, launched in 1986, compares burger prices across countries as a light-hearted guide to whether currencies are over- or undervalued.

ja: 規格化された輸送用コンテナは1950年代にアメリカのマルコム・マクリーンが広め、船の積み下ろしの費用を大きく下げた。
easy: Shipping containers became common in the 1950s. They made moving goods by ship much cheaper.
std: Standardized shipping containers, popularized by Malcom McLean in the 1950s, dramatically reduced the cost of loading and unloading ships.

ja: 世界の貿易品の約8割（量で見て）は船で運ばれている。
easy: About 80% of world trade goods travel by ship.
std: By volume, around 80 percent of global trade is carried by sea.

ja: スエズ運河は1869年に開通し、ヨーロッパとアジアの船の航路を大きく短くした。
easy: The Suez Canal opened in 1869. Ships between Europe and Asia no longer had to go around Africa.
std: The Suez Canal, opened in 1869, allowed ships to travel between Europe and Asia without sailing around Africa.

ja: 日本の消費税は1989年に3％で始まり、1997年に5％、2014年に8％、2019年に10％（食料品などは8％）になった。
easy: Japan's consumption tax started at 3% in 1989. Since 2019, it has been 10%.
std: Japan introduced a 3 percent consumption tax in 1989, raising it to 5 percent in 1997, 8 percent in 2014 and 10 percent in 2019, with a reduced rate for food.

ja: 日本の一万円札の肖像は、2024年に福沢諭吉から「日本資本主義の父」と呼ばれる渋沢栄一に変わった。
easy: Since 2024, Japan's 10,000 yen note shows Shibusawa Eiichi, who started about 500 companies.
std: In 2024, Japan's 10,000-yen note switched its portrait to Shibusawa Eiichi, often called the father of Japanese capitalism for helping found hundreds of companies.

ja: 日本銀行は1882年に設立された。
easy: The Bank of Japan was started in 1882.
std: The Bank of Japan, the country's central bank, was established in 1882.

ja: アメリカの中央銀行制度（FRB）は1913年に作られた。それまでアメリカには長く中央銀行がなかった。
easy: The US central bank system, the Federal Reserve, started in 1913.
std: The Federal Reserve System, the central bank of the United States, was created in 1913.

ja: 日本銀行は2016年に一部の預金の金利をマイナスにした。お金を預けると手数料を取られるような状態で、2024年に終わった。
easy: In 2016, the Bank of Japan started 'negative interest rates'. This ended in 2024.
std: The Bank of Japan introduced a negative interest rate on some bank reserves in 2016 and ended the policy in 2024.

ja: 国際通貨基金（IMF）と世界銀行は、1944年のブレトン・ウッズ会議で設立が決まった。
easy: The IMF and the World Bank were planned at a meeting in Bretton Woods, USA, in 1944.
std: The International Monetary Fund and the World Bank were both created at the Bretton Woods Conference in 1944.

ja: 戦後の日本では1949年から1971年まで、1ドル＝360円の固定相場だった。
easy: From 1949 to 1971, one US dollar was always 360 yen.
std: From 1949 until 1971, the yen was fixed at 360 to the US dollar under the Bretton Woods system.

ja: アップルは1976年に、スティーブ・ジョブズとスティーブ・ウォズニアックらがガレージで始めたとされる。
easy: Apple was started in 1976 by Steve Jobs and Steve Wozniak, famously in a garage.
std: Apple was founded in 1976 by Steve Jobs, Steve Wozniak and Ronald Wayne, with early work famously done in the Jobs family garage.

ja: アップルの創業者の一人ロナルド・ウェインは、創業から12日ほどで自分の持ち分を800ドルで手放した。
easy: One of Apple's first founders sold his share for 800 dollars after about two weeks.
std: Ronald Wayne, Apple's third co-founder, sold his 10 percent stake for 800 dollars about twelve days after the company was formed.

ja: ソニーの前身「東京通信工業」は1946年に創業し、最初の製品の一つは電気炊飯器だったが、うまく売れなかった。
easy: Sony started in 1946. One of its first products was a rice cooker, but it did not sell well.
std: Sony began in 1946 as Tokyo Tsushin Kogyo; one of its first products was an electric rice cooker that failed commercially.

ja: トヨタグループの始まりは豊田佐吉の自動織機。自動車部門は織機会社の一部門として始まった。
easy: Toyota began as a company that made weaving machines.
std: The Toyota group began with Sakichi Toyoda's automatic looms; car-making started as a division of the loom company.

ja: ホンダが最初に売った製品は、自転車に取り付ける小さなエンジンだった。
easy: Honda's first product was a small engine for bicycles.
std: Honda's first product was a small auxiliary engine that could be attached to bicycles.

ja: インスタントラーメンは1958年に安藤百福が発明し、カップヌードルは1971年に発売された。
easy: Instant noodles were invented in Japan in 1958. Cup Noodles came out in 1971.
std: Instant noodles were invented by Momofuku Ando in 1958, and Cup Noodles followed in 1971.

ja: ソニーのウォークマンは1979年に発売された。社内では「録音できないテレコは売れない」と反対の声もあった。
easy: The Sony Walkman came out in 1979. Some people at Sony thought it would not sell.
std: Sony launched the Walkman in 1979, despite internal doubts that a cassette player without recording would sell.

ja: 初代 iPhone は2007年に発表された。
easy: The first iPhone was shown to the world in 2007.
std: The first iPhone was unveiled by Steve Jobs in January 2007.

ja: 写真フィルムで有名だったコダックの技術者は1975年にデジタルカメラを試作したが、会社は主力のフィルム事業を優先した。コダックは2012年に経営破綻した。
easy: An engineer at Kodak made a digital camera in 1975. But Kodak focused on film and went bankrupt in 2012.
std: A Kodak engineer built an early digital camera in 1975, but the company stayed focused on film and filed for bankruptcy in 2012.

ja: レンタルビデオのブロックバスターは、2000年に当時小さかったネットフリックスを5000万ドルで買う機会を断ったと伝えられる。
easy: In 2000, the video rental company Blockbuster reportedly said no to buying Netflix for 50 million dollars.
std: Blockbuster reportedly turned down a chance to buy Netflix for 50 million dollars in 2000; it later went bankrupt while Netflix grew enormously.

ja: 評価額10億ドル以上の未上場のスタートアップを「ユニコーン」と呼ぶ。2013年に投資家のアイリーン・リーが名付けた。
easy: A startup worth over one billion dollars is called a 'unicorn', because it is so rare.
std: A privately held startup valued at over one billion dollars is called a 'unicorn', a term coined by investor Aileen Lee in 2013.

ja: 「ピボット」は事業の方向を大きく変えること。写真共有の Instagram は、もとは位置情報アプリ「Burbn」だった。
easy: Instagram started as a different app called Burbn. Changing direction like this is called a 'pivot'.
std: A 'pivot' is a major change of business direction; Instagram, for example, began as a location check-in app called Burbn.

ja: Slack は、もともとオンラインゲームを作っていたチームが社内で使っていた連絡ツールから生まれた。
easy: Slack started as a chat tool used inside a team that was making a video game.
std: Slack grew out of an internal chat tool used by a team developing an online game that was never commercially successful.

ja: 「ピーターの法則」は、人は能力の限界のポストまで昇進していく、という皮肉な経験則。1969年の本で広まった。
easy: The 'Peter Principle' says people get promoted until they reach a job they cannot do well.
std: The Peter Principle, from a 1969 book, holds that people in a hierarchy tend to be promoted until they reach a level where they are no longer competent.

ja: 「パーキンソンの法則」：仕事は、与えられた時間をすべて使い切るまで膨らむ。1955年の雑誌記事で紹介された。
easy: Parkinson's Law says work grows to fill the time you have for it.
std: Parkinson's law, first stated in a 1955 essay in The Economist, holds that work expands to fill the time available for its completion.

ja: 「自転車置き場の議論」：会議では、大事で難しい議題より、誰でも意見を言いやすい小さな議題に時間がかかりがちという法則。
easy: In meetings, people often spend more time on small, easy topics than on big, hard ones. This is called 'bikeshedding'.
std: 'Bikeshedding', or Parkinson's law of triviality, describes how meetings spend disproportionate time on trivial issues that everyone can comment on.

ja: ポモドーロ・テクニックは25分の作業と5分の休憩を繰り返す時間管理法。名前はトマト型のキッチンタイマーから。
easy: The Pomodoro method means working for 25 minutes and then resting for 5. 'Pomodoro' means tomato in Italian.
std: The Pomodoro Technique alternates 25 minutes of focused work with short breaks; it is named after a tomato-shaped kitchen timer.

ja: アイゼンハワー・マトリクスは、仕事を「緊急か」「重要か」の2つの軸で4つに分けて優先順位を決める方法。
easy: The Eisenhower Matrix puts tasks into four boxes: urgent or not, and important or not.
std: The Eisenhower Matrix sorts tasks into four boxes by urgency and importance to help decide what to do first, delegate, schedule or drop.

ja: 「テレワーク」という言葉は、1970年代のアメリカで石油危機のころに使われ始めた。
easy: The word 'telecommuting' was first used in the 1970s in the US.
std: The term 'telecommuting' was coined in the United States in the 1970s, during the oil crisis.

ja: 日本の「働き方改革関連法」では、2019年から残業時間に原則月45時間・年360時間の上限が設けられた。
easy: Since 2019, Japan's law limits overtime to 45 hours a month in most cases.
std: Under Japan's work-style reform laws, from 2019 overtime has generally been capped at 45 hours a month and 360 hours a year.

ja: フランスでは法律で年5週間の有給休暇が定められている。
easy: In France, workers get five weeks of paid holiday a year by law.
std: French law guarantees employees five weeks of paid annual leave.

ja: アメリカには、国の法律で有給休暇を義務づける制度がない。
easy: The United States has no national law that requires paid holidays for workers.
std: The United States is unusual among rich countries in having no federal law requiring paid vacation.

ja: 「ブランド」の語源は、家畜に押す焼き印（burn と同じ語源）。持ち主を示す印だった。
easy: The word 'brand' first meant a mark burned onto animals to show who owned them.
std: 'Brand' originally referred to a mark burned onto livestock to show ownership, from an old word related to 'burn'.

ja: 「ペルソナ」はマーケティングで、典型的な顧客像を一人の人物として具体的に描いたもの。名前や年齢、悩みまで決める。
easy: In marketing, a 'persona' is an imaginary customer with a name, age, and needs.
std: In marketing, a persona is a detailed fictional profile of a typical customer, including name, age, goals and frustrations.

ja: マーケティングの「4P」は、製品（Product）・価格（Price）・流通（Place）・販促（Promotion）。1960年に提唱された。
easy: The '4 Ps' of marketing are Product, Price, Place, and Promotion.
std: The '4 Ps' of marketing—product, price, place and promotion—were proposed by E. Jerome McCarthy in 1960.

ja: 顧客満足の指標NPSは、「この会社を友人に勧めますか」を0〜10で聞くだけの質問から計算する。
easy: The NPS score asks one question: 'How likely are you to recommend us to a friend?', from 0 to 10.
std: The Net Promoter Score is based on a single question: how likely, on a scale of 0 to 10, a customer is to recommend the company to a friend.

ja: 「A/Bテスト」は、2つの案をランダムに分けた利用者に見せて、どちらがよい結果になるかを比べる方法。
easy: An A/B test shows two versions to different users and checks which one works better.
std: An A/B test randomly shows two versions of something to different users to measure which performs better.

ja: 商品の「ロングテール」：ネット通販では、あまり売れない多くの商品の売上を合わせると、人気商品に匹敵することがある。2004年に広まった考え方。
easy: Online shops can sell many products that are not popular. Together, these can sell as much as the hits. This is the 'long tail'.
std: The 'long tail' idea, popularized in 2004, says online retailers can earn as much from many niche products combined as from a few best-sellers.

ja: 「フリーミアム」は、基本は無料で、高度な機能だけ有料にする商売のやり方。free（無料）と premium（割増）を合わせた言葉。
easy: 'Freemium' means the basic product is free, but extra features cost money.
std: 'Freemium', a blend of 'free' and 'premium', is a business model offering a basic product for free while charging for extra features.

ja: 「ESG投資」は、環境（Environment）・社会（Social）・企業統治（Governance）への取り組みも見て投資先を選ぶ考え方。
easy: ESG investing looks at a company's care for the environment, society, and good management.
std: ESG investing considers a company's environmental, social and governance practices alongside its financial results.
